answer_1.quote: We model KPG as a supervised text generation problem... The input to our model is ... we train the model by minimising the cross-entropy loss between generated and reference key points.
answer_1.outputs: concise key points (abstractive summaries) generated for clusters of arguments

answer_2.quote: We calculate ROUGE scores on the test set... we also compare the performance based on the proposed set-level evaluation approach... Soft-Precision (sP) and Soft-Recall (sR) ... Soft-F1 (sF1) ... We have chosen state-of-the-art semantic similarity evaluation methods such as BLEURT and BARTScore as f_max.

answer_4.quote: Seven annotators were selected... they had to answer a questionnaire containing 66 questions... The annotators were asked to answer on a Likert scale... The first evaluation task (HT1) investigates how well the generated summaries of clusters serve as KPs... Annotators are asked to read three sets of KPs separately (reference, our best approach, previous work), assigning each of the four dimensions above a single score, and then ranking each of the three outputs from best to worst.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate each set of key points on the dimensions VALIDITY, SENTIMENT, INFORMATIVE-NESS, SINGLEASPECT and rank the outputs; additional dimensions such as COVERAGE, REDUNDANCY, SIGNIFICANCE, FAITHFUL-NESS are also evaluated.
